title: Sliding Signed-Claim Protocol for Retry-Resistant Billing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: We observe duplicate billing when clients retry at-least-once requests after timeouts or partial failures. Existing server-side dedupe relies on long-lived global nonces and reconciliation sweeps which are expensive and sometimes fail to prevent short-window duplicate charges. Goal: Introduce a lightweight, backwards-compatible signed-claim protocol that lets clients present short-lived signed usage claims (claims = compact metadata + signature) that the ingestion tier can verify and fast-path to an idempotent accounting ledger, reducing duplicate charges for common retry patterns without increasing storage or global coordination overhead. Design summary: - Clients obtain ephemeral claim tokens from a Claims Issuer (short TTL, e.g., 60s) keyed per customer+client-instance. Tokens contain: customer_id, client_instance_id, sliding-window-seq (small int), ttl, and an HMAC/signature. - For each request, client attaches the current sliding-window-seq and token. The ingestion layer verifies signature and sequence monotonicity within the token's window. - Server maintains a compact in-memory windowed fingerprint cache per customer (bounded by window size and capacity), keyed by token_id+seq, to detect duplicates at ingest time. Cache entries expire slightly after token TTL. Duplicate requests with identical token_id+seq are rejected as duplicate and return a 409 with usage not counted. - When tokens rotate, the issuer allows sequence continuity using a sliding window delta (e.g., last N sequences accepted) to handle clock skew and network jitter. - For clients that cannot get tokens (legacy), fall back to existing global nonce or dedupe-by-receipt flow. - Reconciliation: ingestion still writes provisional reservations; periodic reconciler merges provisional reservations to final charges while dedupe logs are used to suppress recharges of late-arriving duplicates. - Edge cases: out-of-order sequences, lost tokens, multi-path retries handled by accepting a small tolerance and providing reconciliation tools for edge corrections. Why different from current approaches: this is client-assisted, cryptographically signaled idempotency that reduces server coordination surface and storage TTLs. It minimizes false positives/negatives for the common 0-3 retry window without full global commit protocols.
acceptance_criteria: Client SDKs (JS, Python, Go) can request and refresh claim tokens and attach them to generation/embedding requests
Ingest tier validates token signatures and performs fast path duplicate suppression for token_id+seq dedupe (low-latency path <2ms added)
Unit and integration tests cover sequence rollover, token rotation, and out-of-order delivery
Rollback plan: server-side feature flag to disable token validation and fallback to existing dedupe logic with no customer-visible incorrect billing
Telemetry: per-customer duplicate suppression rate, token-issuer latency, claim verification error rate, and reconciliation corrections metric available in Grafana dashboard
notes: 2026-02-28: Kickoff — design sketched during infra sync. Decided to use HMAC tokens signed by Claims Issuer (KMS-protected key).
2026-03-02: Architecture review with PM and Security. Security requested formal threat model; agreed to rotate signing keys and include token binding to customer DSP IDs.
2026-03-04: Prototype results — local bench: 1.8ms median token verification on p95 path, cache hit suppressed duplicates for 87% of simulated 0-3 retry scenarios.
2026-03-06: UX/SDK note — add transparent token refresh and exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd on issuer. JS SDK PR: github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/1421
2026-03-08: PM feedback — include an observability event that links suppressed duplicate to original request ID when available for customer dispute resolution

2026-03-09: Security review (in progress) — requested HSM-backed signing and documented token lifetime rationale. Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Sliding+Signed+Claim+Protocol
2026-03-10: Implementation notes — created feature flag ‘enable_signed_claims’ and server-side config to set window size and cache TTL. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5932
Follow-ups: produce migration runbook for enterprise Private deployments that might have air-gapped Claims Issuer (support offline signing via GRPC signer agent).
